text: Looking in, they saw a quiet room with a glowing fire, a singing kettle, and tea things laid out on the table. <break time="0.8s" /> In the middle of the floor lay the body of Edward Hyde, dressed in clothes far too large for him, clothes of the doctors size. <break time="0.8s" /> A broken little bottle in his hand and a strange smell in the air told them that he had taken poison. <break time="0.8s" /> We have come too late, whether to save or to punish, said Utterson, and now we must find the body of your master. <break time="0.8s" /> They searched every corner of the building, even the dusty cellar, but there was no trace of Henry Jekyll, either dead or alive. <break time="0.8s" /> On the table stood small piles of white salt, which Poole recognized as the same drug that he had always been bringing his master. <break time="0.8s" /> On the desk lay a large envelope addressed to Utterson, and inside was a new will, in which Hydes name had been replaced by Uttersons own. <break time="0.8s" /> There was also a short note, dated that very day, which asked Utterson to read Doctor Lanyons story first and then Jekylls own confession. <break time="0.8s" /> Telling Poole to say nothing yet, Utterson put the sealed packet in his pocket and went back to his office to read the two stories in quiet.
